What the official sources say

  • Residential property is assessed at 9.5% of market value; taxable value is a percent of fair market value, 9.5% for all other property, 11.5% for industrial. (W.S. 39-11-101(a)(xvii); source)
  • The county board of equalization hears the appeal and may affirm the assessor's valuation or find for the taxpayer and remand; written findings are due by October 1 each year. (W.S. 39-13-109(b)(i); source)
  • A taxpayer may appeal a county board of equalization decision to the State Board of Equalization within 30 days of entry of the decision or its legal postmark mailing date, whichever is later. (Dept. of Revenue - Residential (Appeal Process); source)
  • The appeal must address market value, not the tax rate, and must include evidence supporting the owner's estimate of market value. (Dept. of Revenue - Residential (Appeal Process); source)
  • An action to enjoin an illegal assessment, levy or collection must be filed in district court within one year following the illegal assessment, levy or collection. (W.S. 39-13-109(c)(i); source)
  • The county treasurer advertises a real property tax sale once a week for three weeks in a legal newspaper, first publication at least four weeks before the sale. (W.S. 39-13-108(e)(ii)(A); source)
  • Sales are held at the county courthouse between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.; the person offering to pay the taxes, interest, penalties and costs is the purchaser and receives a certificate of purchase. (W.S. 39-13-108(e)(iii); source)

Who sets and collects property tax in Wyoming?

In Wyoming, the county assessor values property, local governments set the mill levies, and the county treasurer collects the money. The state Department of Revenue Property Tax Division supports and trains the local offices and assesses public utility property such as pipelines, railroads and telecommunications. It also tells homeowners not to pay residential tax to the division, so payments go to your county treasurer.

The Legislature sets the assessment ratio. Residential property is assessed at 9.5 percent of market value, industrial property at 11.5 percent and minerals at 100 percent of fair market value. Local bodies such as school districts, hospital districts, towns and counties then levy the mills they need to fund their budgets.

That split matters when you sell. Your valuation comes from one office, your rate from several taxing districts, and your bill from a third. If a number looks wrong, you need to know which office to call.

How do you calculate a Wyoming property tax bill?

The formula is market value times the assessment ratio times the mill levy divided by 1,000, and one mill equals $1 per $1,000 of assessed value. A $100,000 home in the Laramie County example from Better Wyoming owes about $722 at a 76 mill total levy.

The 2025 statewide numbers give some context for what homeowners carry:

2025 measureFigure
Total assessed valuationAbout $27.65 billion
Total property taxes leviedAbout $1.805 billion
Statewide average mill levy65.280 mills
Residential share of assessed valueAbout 30 percent
Mineral share of assessed valueAbout 44 percent
Lowest county average levyTeton, 57.772 mills
Highest county average levyBig Horn, 73.826 mills

Natrona County averaged 72.238 mills and Weston County 73.210. The spread shows why moving a few miles can change what a buyer pays each year on a house of the same value.

What is the 25 percent residential exemption?

The 25 percent exemption, created by Senate Enrolled Act 60 in 2025, cuts the taxable value of a home by 25 percent on fair market value up to $1 million. It has no expiration date, and the bill did not include backfill money for special districts, local governments or schools that lose revenue.

Eligibility is limited to owner-occupied houses, condominiums, townhouses and manufactured homes where the owner lives at least eight months a year. Some military members who cannot meet the eight-month rule may still qualify. Owners file an affidavit with the county assessor, and the filing deadline in the second year was March 1 after the Department of Revenue extended it from February 1. Homeowners using the long-term homeowners exemption do not qualify for the 25 percent reduction until tax year 2027.

A separate bill that would have changed how acquisition value is used in residential assessment passed the House 35 to 25 but failed in the Senate Committee of the Whole 8 to 21 on February 28, 2025.

What other relief programs can lower a Wyoming tax bill?

Wyoming has a refund program, a veteran exemption and a senior reduction in addition to the 25 percent exemption. Each has its own application and its own office, so check which ones a seller already has on file.

  • Property tax refund: for homeowners who struggle to pay. Households at or below 125 percent of county median income receive 75 percent of taxes paid, capped at half the county's median residential bill. The ceiling is 145 percent of county median income, and those between 126 and 145 percent receive that amount reduced by 35 percent.
  • Veteran exemption: rose from $3,000 to $6,000 in 2024.
  • Senior relief: Wyomingites 65 or older who have paid Wyoming property tax for at least 25 years receive a 50 percent cut.
  • The 2025 Legislature added $10.5 million to the refund program, and the Better Wyoming FAQ says that funding expires after 2026.

The refund application site is wptrs.wyo.gov. Applications for the 2025 round closed June 2.

When is the valuation date, and how does a Wyoming assessment appeal start?

Wyoming property is listed, valued and assessed as of January 1, and an appeal begins with the county assessor. Laramie County states that assessment schedules are mailed no later than the fourth Monday in April, and that written objections must reach the assessor within 30 days of the mailing date.

The county board of equalization decides current-year protests in writing by October 1, and under W.S. 39-13-109(b)(i) it can affirm the assessor or find for the taxpayer. Further appeals go to the State Board of Equalization and then to district court, as described in the statute.

The Department of Revenue says an appeal must address market value, not the tax rate, and must include evidence supporting your estimate. Useful evidence for a house you are about to sell includes a recent appraisal, photos of defects the assessor may not have seen, and any signed purchase contract showing what a buyer will pay.

When is Wyoming property tax due, and what does late payment cost?

Tax is paid in two halves, due by November 10 and May 10, and late balances accrue interest at 18 percent per year. Laramie County mails notices the last business day of August. The first half is due September 1 and payable by November 10, and the second half is due March 1 and payable by May 10 of the next year.

If you pay the entire bill by December 31, the interest on the first half is waived. The county treasurer certifies a delinquent list if taxes remain unpaid after May 11, and a demand notice goes out about five business days later. Unpaid taxes are still owed even if you never received the bill.

Many owners pay through a mortgage escrow account. The Laramie County treasurer says that if both the lender and the owner pay, the treasurer keeps the first payment and refunds the duplicate. Before listing a house, confirm with the treasurer that the escrow payment actually posted.

What happens if Wyoming property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid real property tax becomes a perpetual lien on the property, and the county can sell it at a tax sale. Under W.S. 39-13-108, the lien ranks against all persons except the United States and the State of Wyoming.

  • The treasurer advertises the sale once a week for three weeks in a legal newspaper, with the first notice at least four weeks before the sale.
  • Sales take place at the county courthouse between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., excluding Sundays.
  • The buyer who pays the taxes, interest, penalties and costs receives a certificate of purchase.
  • If the property does not sell for the amount owed, the county treasurer bids it in for the county.
  • A tax deed can issue for unredeemed property four years after the sale, after notice to occupants, owners and mortgagees at least three months beforehand.

The version of the statute we reviewed is dated 2012, so confirm current details with your treasurer. The takeaway holds either way: the sooner you resolve a delinquency, the more options you keep.

How do you handle Wyoming property tax when you sell?

The simplest approach is to get a payoff figure from the county treasurer and have it paid from sale proceeds at closing. Because the tax is a lien on the real property, it stays with the house until paid.

The deed itself is recorded with the county clerk with a sworn statement from the grantee or the grantee's agent, as W.S. 34-1-142 requires. That statement discloses the price and terms but is kept confidential, and it may be shown only to someone reviewing or contesting a property tax assessment.

After a sale, check whether the 25 percent exemption or any other exemption stays in place. The exemption depends on the owner living in the house, so the buyer may have to file their own affidavit. If you inherited the house or are selling after a death, the small estate limit rose to $400,000 on July 1, 2025, which can speed up transfer when real property is part of a modest estate.

More questions about Wyoming Property Tax Guide

What percent of market value is Wyoming residential property assessed at?

Residential property is assessed at 9.5 percent of market value. Industrial property is 11.5 percent and minerals are 100 percent.

What is the Wyoming average mill levy?

The statewide average was 65.280 mills for the 2025 tax year. County averages ranged from 57.772 in Teton County to 73.826 in Big Horn County.

How do I qualify for the 25 percent homeowner exemption?

You must own and live in the home at least eight months of the year and file an affidavit with your county assessor. The exemption covers 25 percent of fair market value up to $1 million.

What interest does Wyoming charge on late property tax?

Delinquent balances accrue 18 percent interest per year. Paying the whole bill by December 31 waives interest on the first half.

Where do I appeal a Wyoming property assessment?

File with the county assessor within 30 days of the assessment schedule notice. The county board of equalization hears it and decides by October 1.
